text: In Mexico City, elderly women living alone were being found dead in their own homes. Many seem to have let their killer in.
They had opened the door themselves.
The killings began in the late nineteen nineties. By two thousand five, the city was in a panic. The press gave the killer a name: La Mah-tah-vee-eh-hee-tahs. The little old lady killer.
text0: The killings began in the late 1990s. By 2005, the city was in a panic. The press gave the killer a name: La Mataviejitas. The little old lady killer.

text: Investigators believed the killer posed as a government worker, offering pensions and welfare programs, to get through the door.
Witnesses described a tall, masculine-looking woman. Police decided they were hunting a man in disguise, and swept through the city's transgender community.
For a time, officials even dismissed talk of a serial killer as media sensationalism. The deaths kept coming.
One lead went somewhere strange: several victims owned the same print of a painting, a boy in a red waistcoat. It was only a coincidence.
Police were looking for the wrong person.
On January twenty-fifth, two thousand six, a woman was caught fleeing the home of an eighty-two-year-old victim, Ah-nah Mah-ree-ah de los Reh-yes Al-fah-ro.
text0: On January 25, 2006, a woman was caught fleeing the home of an eighty-two-year-old victim, Ana María de los Reyes Alfaro.

text: Her name was Wah-nah Bah-rah-sah. Born in Ee-dahl-go in nineteen fifty-seven, she had survived a brutal childhood with an alcoholic mother.
text0: Her name was Juana Barraza. Born in Hidalgo in 1957, she had survived a brutal childhood with an alcoholic mother.

text: On weekends, she was a professional wrestler: La Dah-mah del See-len-see-oh. The Lady of Silence.
text0: On weekends, she was a professional wrestler: La Dama del Silencio. The Lady of Silence.

text: Her fingerprints linked her to at least ten crime scenes. She admitted to four killings, and said her motive was resentment toward her own mother.
In two thousand eight, she was convicted of sixteen murders and sentenced to seven hundred and fifty-nine years.
text0: In 2008, she was convicted of sixteen murders and sentenced to 759 years.

text: Authorities linked her to as many as forty deaths. After her arrest, dozens of cases were simply closed… some of them never solved.
The killer everyone was looking for… was the one nobody suspected. This is Plot Twist, with A. and R.
